name: SSH
description: Lists the hosts in your ssh config and opens an ssh session in a new terminal, through bastion hosts when you name them. Inside a session, commands show as blocks through a shell integration that lives only for that session. With your consent per host, a small helper script under ~/.ostia there gives {product} that host's files. A session an agent asks for opens only after you approve the exact command.

commands.title: SSH: Connect to Host…
commands.argument: Host, as you would type it after ssh: [-J bastion] [-p port] [user@]host

commands.title: User, host name, port and bastion hops of one host (JSON)
SSH: Install Remote Helper on Host…
commands.argument: Host, as you would type it after ssh: [-J bastion] [-p port] [user@]host

commands.title: SSH: Remove Remote Helper…
commands.argument: Host to remove the helper from, as you would type it after ssh

commands.title: Hosts you answered the remote helper question for (JSON)

shellIntegration.title: Shell integration in ssh sessions
shellIntegration.description: Command blocks and the current folder inside bash and zsh sessions: ssh runs with -t and a fixed command that writes a private temporary folder on the host, sources it as the shell starts and deletes it at once. Nothing is installed. Turn it off for hosts that refuse a remote command

remoteHelper.title: Remote helper
remoteHelper.description: Offer to install a small helper script under ~/.ostia on a host, which gives {product} that host's files over ssh. You are asked once per host, with the exact path, before anything is installed. Turn it off to never ask and never connect
